thread.title: Stock Futures Edge Up: 'Avengers' Lifts Disney, Beauty Name Eyes Breakout

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stock Futures Edge Up: 'Avengers' Lifts Disney, Beauty Name Eyes Breakout
text:
Stock futures pointed modestly higher Monday as Sprint ( S ) and T-Mobile ( TMUS ) merger news, a Walt Disney ( DIS ) film release and strong first-quarter results from McDonald's ( MCD ) helped determine early trade.
X Stock futures for the Dow Jones industrial average maintained a 0.5% advance as advancers led decliners by a wide margin in premarket trading. McDonald's took the mantle from Disney to pace an early lead.
S&P 500 futures gained 0.4%. Nasdaq 100 futures were off early highs, trading 0.5% above fair value. Ulta Beauty ( ULTA ) and Charter Communications ( CHTR ) led the Nasdaq's the upside, and T-Mobile posting the largest decline in premarket trading.
The Nasdaq has finished the last six weeks, while the Dow and S&P 500 the last seven weeks, below their 50-day moving averages. This and a number of other critical factors, such as distribution days, have placed the market's four-week-old uptrend under pressure . But although the market's progress has been stalled since February, its current pullback remains mild. The Dow is almost 9% below, the S&P 500 down 7% from their highs, both marked on Jan. 26. The Nasdaq is less than 7% below its March 13 high-water mark. All three indexes open Monday within about 1% of their 50-day lines.
Sprint, T-Mobile Merge; McDonald's Beats; Ulta Beauty Teases Breakout Shares of Sprint dived 14% and T-Mobile slipped more than 2% after the two wireless carriers agreed to a $26.5 billion merger . Walmart ( WMT ) inched ahead 0.4% after announcing plans to sell its Britain-based Asda Group to grocery chain Sainsbury for $10.3 billion. The deal — which must pass muster with British regulators — would merge the country's second and third largest grocery chains. Walmart would reportedly retain ownership of 42% of the combined company.
But McDonald's and Walt Disney were the prime early movers among Dow Jones stocks. McDonald's powered up 4.1% after first-quarter results easily topped analysts' estimates . The stock is struggling to hold support at its 10-week moving average.
Disney's "Avengers: Infinity War" rumbled into the summer movie season with a $630 million box office take worldwide. About $250 million of that coming from North American theaters. The roll up of Marvel super heroes set opening weekend records in both regional categories. China, the second-largest box office market worldwide, was not included in the numbers. The film is set to debut there on May 11.
Disney traded up 1.6% ahead of Monday's open. But shares recently have been less than heroic, flagging 12% from a January high and trapped below their 10-week moving average since February.

Please contact customer service CLOSE A week with a powerful slate of earnings news includes reports from Apple ( AAPL ) on Tuesday, and from a long-list of energy stocks such as EOG Resources ( EOG ), Noble Energy ( NBL ) and Matador Resources ( MTDR ).
Ulta Beauty rose 1.6%, one of the best premarket gains among Nasdaq 100 names. The beauty supply and salon chain is sitting atop a four-week advance, up 30% from an early March high and just below a 249.40 buy point in a cup base . The premarket move positioned Ulta shares to open above that buy point. Not all premarket moves carry over into regular trade.
GrubHub ( GRUB ) pared an early 5% to around 3% in premarket trading. The online takeout food ordering app last week narrowed a 9% decline to around 2%. The stock is six-weeks into a consolidation, with the company due to report first-quarter results on Tuesday.
Economic News: Consumer Spending, Price Data On Target; Incomes Lag An important week for economic news begins with key inflation data early Monday and ramps toward the Labor Department's closely-watched April payrolls report, due Friday morning.
Consumer prices gauges for March came in at or slightly below economists' targets, a positive for those concerned about inflation pressures. The Commerce Department's Personal Consumption and Expenditure Price Index was flat, below targets of 0.1% growth. Core prices, minus energy and food, rose 0.2%, in line with estimates. Consumer spending rose 0.4%, meeting expectations. The weak spot was personal income growth, up 0.3% and lagging estimates for a 0.4% gain.
Also on Monday's schedule: the Chicago purchasing managers index at 9:45 a.m. ET, March pending home sales from the National Association of Realtors at 10 a.m. ET and the Dallas Federal Reserve Bank's regional manufacturing survey at 10:30 a.m. ET.
